title: Cardinal Billing Account Standing Rules: Returned Payments, Certified Funds and Failed Autopay Drafts
content:
**Rule.** When a posted payment on a Cardinal Billing Account is returned unpaid, its credit is reversed in full and the pay plan's returned-payment fee is charged, tied to the returned payment. Each returned payment carries exactly one fee, including a re-presented autopay draft that fails again.

**Effect on earlier relief.** A returned payment counts as never received, so a notice rescission or reinstatement that relied on it is undone by the system.

**Certified funds.** When the account reaches the pay plan's returned-payment limit within the pay plan's lookback months (counting returned payments in the rolling months ending on the date of the latest return), only certified funds (cashier's check, money order or debit card) are accepted for the pay plan's certified-funds months from the latest return. The last day of that period is recorded on the account as the certified-funds end date.

**Autopay drafts.** On an autopay plan a failed draft is re-presented after the pay plan's retry days, as many times as the pay plan's number of re-presentments. When failed drafts in the lookback (returned payments whose original payment was an autopay draft) reach the pay plan's failed-draft limit, autopay is removed and the account moves to the plan of the pay plan's fallback rank.

**Phone payments.** A returned payment of a payment made by a representative over the phone is handled the same way.

## Condition and result table

| Condition on the account | Result |
|---|---|
| A posted payment is returned unpaid | Its credit is reversed in full; one returned-payment fee is charged, tied to it |
| A re-presented autopay draft fails again | It is a further returned payment and carries its own fee |
| A rescission or reinstatement relied on the returned payment | It is undone by the system |
| Returned payments in the lookback reach the plan limit | Certified funds only, for the plan's certified-funds months from the latest return |
| Failed autopay drafts in the lookback reach the plan's failed-draft limit | Autopay removed; account moved to the fallback plan |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical)

A Cardinal Card Autopay Monthly Plan draft of $120.00 fails. Its $120.00 credit is reversed and one returned-payment fee is charged. The draft is re-presented after the plan's retry days and fails again: that second return is reversed too and carries its own fee. If those are the account's second failed drafts within the lookback and the plan's failed-draft limit is two, autopay is removed and the account moves to the fallback plan; and with two returned payments within the lookback the account is also limited to certified funds from the latest return when the plan's returned-payment limit is two.
